description: This bar chart, titled “comparison by language family” from the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models,” illustrates the performance comparison between two multilingual models—mBERT and XLM-R—across various language families, measured by “task count” on the y-axis, which ranges from 0 to 40 in increments of 10. The x-axis lists language families in the following order: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. For each language family, three bars are displayed: light blue for “mBERT better,” dark blue for “XLM-R better,” and light green for “same,” as indicated by the legend in the upper right. In most categories, XLM-R outperforms mBERT (dark blue bars are taller), with the most pronounced advantage in IE-Slavic (dark blue ≈ 39), followed by IE-Romance (≈13) and IE-Germanic (≈18). The “same” category (light green) is notably high in IE-Romance (≈30) and IE-Slavic (≈28), suggesting strong agreement between models in those families. mBERT only clearly outperforms XLM-R in IE-Slavic (light blue ≈12) and IE-Romance (≈4), and slightly in IE-Germanic (≈4). The “same” category is lowest for Isolate and Semitic (≈1 each), while XLM-R dominates in Uralic (≈14) and Semitic (≈7). The chart visually emphasizes XLM-R’s overall superior performance across most language families, with IE-Slavic showing the largest absolute task count and the most balanced comparison between models.
